architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created a standalone troubleshooting guide instead of updating existing documentation files, and added it to the documentation navigation structure
architecture_decisions.rationale: The troubleshooting content is extensive (200+ lines) and covers multiple distinct problem domains (Stripe, URLs, Docker, API v2, SSL). A standalone guide provides better organization and discoverability than scattering updates across multiple existing docs. Adding it to docs.json ensures it appears in the documentation navigation, making it accessible to users.
alternatives_considered: Updating existing self-hosting documentation files piecemeal
Adding troubleshooting sections to each relevant existing guide
Creating a GitHub wiki page instead of integrated documentation

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Documented specific error scenarios with clear symptoms, causes, and solutions, focusing on actionable fixes
architecture_decisions.rationale: Troubleshooting documentation is most effective when it follows a pattern: symptom → cause → solution. This structure helps users quickly identify their issue and apply the fix. The guide includes specific error messages (CLIENT_FETCH_ERROR), environment variable names, and Docker service names that match actual codebase behavior.
alternatives_considered: Generic troubleshooting advice without specific error messages
Only listing solutions without explaining causes
Creating separate guides for each error type

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Clarified environment variable requirements across different deployment contexts (Docker, Vercel, API v2)
architecture_decisions.rationale: The codebase has complex configuration requirements with environment variables spread across .env, .env.appStore, and service-specific requirements. The guide addresses common pitfalls: build-time vs runtime variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL), optional vs required variables (NEXTAUTH_URL), and service-specific requirements (API v2 environment variables not in root .env.example).
alternatives_considered: Listing all environment variables without context
Assuming users will read all .env.example files
Not distinguishing between different deployment methods

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Documented API v2 service requirements and environment variable discrepancies
architecture_decisions.rationale: API v2 (NestJS) has different environment variable requirements than the main web app, and missing variables cause service crashes. The guide explicitly lists required API v2 variables and notes that STRIPE_API_KEY is the v2 equivalent of STRIPE_PRIVATE_KEY, addressing a common point of confusion in the dual-API architecture.
alternatives_considered: Treating all environment variables uniformly across services

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Provided secure alternatives to disabling TLS verification and explained the risks
architecture_decisions.rationale: The guide addresses SSL/TLS issues behind reverse proxies by recommending proper header forwarding (X-Forwarded-Proto) instead of disabling certificate verification. It explicitly warns against NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 for production and explains the security risks, aligning with the codebase's security-conscious architecture.
alternatives_considered: Simply recommending to disable TLS verification
Not addressing SSL issues at all

tickets.title: Create comprehensive self-hosting troubleshooting guide
tickets.description: Create a new troubleshooting guide that addresses common deployment issues reported in GitHub issues, covering Stripe configuration, URL redirects, Docker-specific problems, API v2 service requirements, and SSL/TLS configuration

implementation_summary:
The implementation creates a comprehensive troubleshooting guide for self-hosted Cal.com deployments, addressing gaps identified from real user issues (referenced GitHub issues #25993, #21921). The guide follows a structured approach: each section identifies a specific symptom, explains the root cause, and provides actionable solutions with code examples.

Key patterns used include: 1) Problem-solution structure for quick troubleshooting, 2) Clear differentiation between deployment contexts (Docker vs Vercel, API v1 vs API v2), 3) Emphasis on security best practices (avoiding NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 in production), and 4) Reference to existing codebase patterns (environment variable organization, service architecture).

The guide integrates with the existing documentation system by being added to docs.json's navigation structure under the self-hosting section. It complements rather than replaces existing documentation, focusing specifically on troubleshooting scenarios that users encounter during deployment. The content reflects actual codebase behavior, such as the API v2 service's strict environment variable requirements and the dual Stripe key configuration (STRIPE_PRIVATE_KEY for web, STRIPE_API_KEY for API v2).
